To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for large traffic networks with millions of nodes, the preprocessing time can be reduced by a factor of 2, the space consumption can be reduced by 50%, and the online computation time can be reduced significantly (up to a factor of 20) by using geometric speed-up techniques.

the geometric speed-up technique can reduce the response time significantly, that the geometric objects that are best for this are the so-called “sweeping cones” that contain all nodes that can lie on a shortest path that starts with an edge of the cone, and that the geometric speed up technique is especially useful if the layout of the graph can be computed efficiently.

the preprocessing time for our algorithm can be as low as 0.5 seconds for graphs with 1.5 million nodes, that the online response time for a typical query can be as low for as 0.02 seconds, and that the memory requirement for storing the result of the precomputation is 1.3 MB for a graph with 1.2 million nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to use the layout of a graph for speeding up the search for shortest paths?
the following questions: Which geometric objects are most suitable?
the question: How to use a layout to reduce the search space in Dijkstra’s algorithm?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for traffic networks, the use of geometric objects is a good idea, but that the choice of the geometric object type is not so important.
the geometric speed-up techniques are very promising for large traffic networks.
, in our experiments, the geometric objects that are based on the layout of the network are superior to the other types of geometric objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geometric speed-up techniques we present can reduce the response time by a factor of about 2.
for the considered problem instance, the best results were obtained by using the union of the Voronoi cells of the source and the target as search space.
the geometric speed-up techniques can be very efficient for large sparse graphs, but that they depend on the type of the geometric object and on the structure of the graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of geometric objects can speed up the online computation of shortest paths by more than a factor of 10.
the choice of geometric objects is very important.
the use of geometric objects is a promising approach to improve the efficiency of shortest path algorithms.
